points.place: 英国多塞特郡莱姆里杰斯
points.title: 童年与化石启蒙
points.description: 玛丽·安宁1799年出生于英国多塞特郡的海滨小镇莱姆里杰斯，是家中十个孩子中的老大。她的父亲理查德·安宁是一名木匠兼化石收集者，经常带着孩子们在附近的悬崖和海滩上寻找化石。玛丽从小就跟随父亲学习化石识别和收集技巧。然而，在1800年，她的父亲不幸去世，家庭陷入贫困。为了维持生计，玛丽和她的哥哥约瑟夫开始继续在海滩上寻找化石并将其卖给游客，这成为他们家庭的主要收入来源。
points.descriptionEn: Mary Anning was born in 1799 in Lyme Regis, a coastal town in Dorset, England, as the eldest of ten children. Her father Richard Anning was a carpenter and fossil collector who often took his children to search for fossils along the nearby cliffs and beaches. Mary learned fossil identification and collecting techniques from her father at a young age. However, in 1800, her father tragically passed away, plunging the family into poverty. To make ends meet, Mary and her brother Joseph continued searching for fossils on the beaches and selling them to tourists, which became their primary source of income.

points.place: 英国多塞特郡莱姆里杰斯
points.title: 发现蛇颈龙化石
points.description: 1811年，12岁的玛丽和她哥哥约瑟夫在莱姆里杰斯附近的黑维崖(Black Ven)悬崖上发现了一具几乎完整的蛇颈龙化石。这具化石长约5.2米，是当时发现的最完整的史前海洋爬行动物化石之一。约瑟夫最初发现了头骨部分，随后玛丽在接下来的几个月里仔细挖掘并收集了其余部分。这一发现引起了科学界的广泛关注，化石最终被伦敦的英国自然历史博物馆收藏。这次发现不仅为玛丽带来了收入，也让她开始被科学界所注意，尽管当时女性在科学领域几乎没有地位。
points.descriptionEn: In 1811, at the age of 12, Mary and her brother Joseph discovered a nearly complete ichthyosaur fossil on the cliffs of Black Ven near Lyme Regis. The fossil was about 5.2 meters long and was one of the most complete prehistoric marine reptile fossils discovered at the time. Joseph initially found the skull portion, and Mary then carefully excavated and collected the rest of the specimen over the following months. This discovery garnered significant attention from the scientific community, and the fossil was eventually acquired by the British Museum of Natural History in London. This find not only brought Mary income but also began to attract notice from the scientific community, although women had virtually no status in science at the time.

points.place: 英国多塞特郡莱姆里杰斯
points.title: 发现鱼龙与蛇颈龙化石
points.description: 1820年，玛丽发现了一具完整的鱼龙化石，这是她首次独立发现的重要化石。随后在1823年，她发现了一具独特的蛇颈龙化石，这种后来被称为'安宁蛇颈龙'(Plesiosaurus anningae)的物种具有长颈和小头，与之前发现的蛇颈龙有明显区别。这一发现引起了英国著名地质学家威廉·巴克兰的注意，他后来成为玛丽的重要支持者。玛丽通过这些发现积累了丰富的古生物学知识，尽管她没有接受过正规教育，但她对化石的观察力和解剖学理解令人惊叹。这些发现使她成为当时英国最著名的化石收藏家之一。
points.descriptionEn: In 1820, Mary discovered a complete ichthyosaur fossil, her first major independent discovery. Then in 1823, she discovered a unique plesiosaur fossil, a species later named 'Plesiosaurus anningae' with its distinctive long neck and small head, clearly different from previously discovered ichthyosaurs. This discovery caught the attention of renowned British geologist William Buckland, who later became an important supporter of Mary. Through these finds, Mary accumulated extensive paleontological knowledge, and despite her lack of formal education, her observational skills and anatomical understanding were remarkable. These discoveries established her as one of Britain's most prominent fossil collectors of the time.

points.place: 英国多塞特郡莱姆里杰斯
points.title: 发现飞鱼龙化石
points.description: 1830年，玛丽发现了一具独特的飞鱼龙(翼龙)化石，这是英国发现的第一个完整的翼龙化石。这具化石具有翼展约1.5米，保存了翼膜和头冠的细节，为科学家提供了关于这种远古飞行生物的重要信息。这一发现再次证明了玛丽非凡的化石识别能力。然而，由于当时科学界对女性科学家的偏见，玛丽的研究成果常常被男性科学家发表，而她的贡献很少被承认。尽管如此，她的发现为早期古生物学研究提供了关键证据，帮助科学家理解地球历史上的生物多样性。
points.descriptionEn: In 1830, Mary discovered a unique pterosaur fossil, the first complete pterosaur fossil found in Britain. The fossil had a wingspan of about 1.5 meters and preserved details of the wing membranes and crest, providing important information about this ancient flying creature. This discovery once again demonstrated Mary's exceptional fossil identification skills. However, due to the scientific community's bias against female scientists at the time, Mary's research findings were often published by male scientists while her contributions were rarely acknowledged. Nevertheless, her discoveries provided crucial evidence for early paleontological research, helping scientists understand the biodiversity of Earth's prehistoric past.

points.place: 英国多塞特郡莱姆里杰斯
points.title: 晚年与科学认可
points.description: 1835年，玛丽得到了英国地质学会的一笔小额年金，这是对她工作的首次正式认可。然而，由于她是女性，她无法加入该学会。在晚年，玛丽继续在莱姆里杰斯的海滩上寻找化石，尽管健康状况逐渐恶化。1847年，玛丽因乳腺癌去世，年仅47岁。尽管她在世时没有得到应有的科学认可，但她的发现对古生物学产生了深远影响。她收集的化石帮助建立了地球历史上生物演化的证据，支持了查尔斯·达尔文后来提出的进化论。玛丽去世后，她的贡献逐渐被重新认识，她被视为早期女性科学家的先驱，打破了当时社会对女性参与科学研究的限制。
points.descriptionEn: In 1835, Mary received a small annuity from the Geological Society of London, the first official recognition of her work. However, as a woman, she was not permitted to join the society. In her later years, Mary continued searching for fossils on the beaches of Lyme Regis despite her declining health. She died of breast cancer in 1847 at the age of 47. Although she did not receive proper scientific recognition during her lifetime, her discoveries had a profound impact on paleontology. The fossils she collected helped establish evidence for the evolution of life on Earth, supporting Charles Darwin's later theory of evolution. After her death, Mary's contributions were gradually re-evaluated, and she is now recognized as a pioneer of early female scientists who broke through the societal restrictions on women's participation in scientific research.

appraisal.zh: 玛丽·安宁如今被公认为古生物学的先驱和自学成才的典范：她凭借非凡的观察力发现多处重要化石，为早期古生物学乃至后来的进化论提供了关键证据，其经历也激励了后世女性投身科学。不过也有研究者指出，她缺乏正规科学训练，对化石的解读有其局限，重要发现常由男性科学家重新解释发表，她生前所得认可有限，其地位在相当程度上是后人的建构。
appraisal.en: Mary Anning is now widely recognized as a pioneer of paleontology and a self-taught exemplar: her extraordinary observational skills yielded several important fossil finds that provided crucial evidence for early paleontology and later evolutionary theory, and her story has inspired women to pursue science. Yet some researchers note that without formal training her interpretations were limited, that male scientists often reinterpreted and published her discoveries, and that she received little recognition in her lifetime, her present standing being largely a later construction.

supporter.zh: 玛丽·安宁被视为古生物学领域的先驱和女性科学家的典范。她自学成才，在没有正规教育的情况下，凭借非凡的观察力和毅力，发现了多个重要史前生物化石，为早期古生物学研究提供了关键证据。她的工作不仅丰富了人类对地球历史的认识，也为后来的进化论提供了支持。玛丽的故事激励了无数女性投身科学事业，打破了19世纪社会对女性参与科学研究的限制。她的坚韧、求知精神和专业能力使她成为科学史上不可忽视的人物。
supporter.en: Mary Anning is regarded as a pioneer in paleontology and a role model for female scientists. Self-taught without formal education, she demonstrated extraordinary observational skills and perseverance, discovering several important prehistoric fossils that provided crucial evidence for early paleontological research. Her work not only enriched humanity's understanding of Earth's history but also supported the later development of evolutionary theory. Mary's story has inspired countless women to pursue scientific careers, breaking through 19th-century societal restrictions on women's participation in scientific research. Her resilience, intellectual curiosity, and professional abilities make her an indispensable figure in scientific history.

critic.zh: 批评者指出，玛丽·安宁虽然发现了许多重要化石，但由于缺乏正规科学训练，她对化石的解读和理解存在局限性。她的发现常常被男性科学家重新解释和发表，而她本人很少获得应有的学术认可。此外，玛丽的经济状况一直不稳定，她被迫出售化石以维持生计，这导致许多重要标本最终落入私人收藏而非公共机构，限制了科学研究的广泛获取。批评者也认为，玛丽在科学界的地位更多是后人的建构，而非她生前获得的实际认可。
critic.en: Critics point out that while Mary Anning discovered many important fossils, her lack of formal scientific training limited her ability to interpret and understand them fully. Her discoveries were often reinterpreted and published by male scientists while she received little academic recognition for her work. Additionally, Mary's financial instability forced her to sell fossils to make a living, which meant many important specimens ended up in private collections rather than public institutions, limiting broad scientific access. Critics also argue that Mary's status in scientific history is largely a posthumous construction rather than the recognition she actually received during her lifetime.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，玛丽·安宁被定义为一位突破性别界限的科学家和自学成才的天才。她的故事反映了19世纪科学界对女性的系统性排斥，同时也展示了个人才华如何能在不利环境中绽放。现代科学史重新评价了她的贡献，承认她不仅是化石收集者，更是真正的古生物学先驱。她的生平成为科学教育的重要案例，被广泛用于讨论性别平等、科学民主化和非传统教育路径的价值。在流行文化中，她已成为女性赋权和科学探索的象征。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Mary Anning is defined as a scientist who broke gender barriers and a self-taught genius. Her story reflects the systematic exclusion of women from 19th-century science while demonstrating how individual talent can flourish despite adverse circumstances. Modern historiography has re-evaluated her contributions, recognizing her not merely as a fossil collector but as a true pioneer of paleontology. Her life has become a significant case study in science education, widely used to discuss gender equality, the democratization of science, and the value of non-traditional educational paths. In popular culture, she has become a symbol of female empowerment and scientific exploration.

self.zh: 我卖掉我的化石是为了养活我的母亲和兄弟。科学是好的，但面包是必要的。
self.en: I sell my fossils to feed my mother and brothers. Science is good, but bread is necessary.
